hero.lead: A nation of 14.6 million on hills three-quarters farmed, that earned $685 million from visitors in 2025 and registered $2.62 billion of new investment.

capital.heading: Rwanda borrows on reforms it can show. Next, a clean stove in every home.

record.text: Overall public debt as a share of GDP in 2025, which the IMF expects to be the peak; risk of debt distress moderate
IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved June 2026, 38 months
Commercial financing the World Bank Group guarantee of March 2026 can mobilize: €213 million closed in April and EUR 82 million and JPY 15 billion on 26 August 2026
Energy Sector Results Based Financing Phase II, $200 million from the AfDB and $100 million from AIIB: 200,000 households to the grid and clean cooking for 100,000
World Bank support to electricity and clean cooking access (ASCENT), approved November 2023

register.name: Dual-currency commercial loan, euro and yen
register.detail: Closed 26 August 2026 · EUR 82 million and JPY 15 billion · 15 years, 6 years’ grace · IDA policy-based guarantee as first loss, MIGA cover as second loss
register.note: Under the World Bank Group Guarantee Platform, housed at MIGA
register.text: A two-tranche commercial loan from Société Générale and Standard Chartered Bank for general budgetary purposes, in line with the World Bank’s Inclusive and Resilient Job Creation operation. World Bank Group cover lets Rwanda borrow for 15 years, which leaves more room in the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: Commercial loan under World Bank Group guarantees
register.detail: Closed April 2026 · 15 years, six years’ grace · IDA policy-based guarantee and MIGA second-loss guarantee cover 95% of debt service
register.note: About $243 million (Ministry of Finance)
register.text: A commercial loan from Société Générale and Standard Chartered whose debt service is 95% covered by an IDA policy-based guarantee and a MIGA second-loss guarantee. It draws on the World Bank Group guarantee approved in March 2026.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 8 June 2026 · 38 months
register.note: SDR 185.031 million; first review agreed at staff level, 6 October 2026
register.text: The first IMF lending arrangement since the Standby Credit Facility. Completion of the first review would release about $35.7 million.

register.name: Access to Finance for Recovery and Resilience, second additional financing
register.detail: Approved 21 May 2026 · IDA credit · Implemented by the Development Bank of Rwanda
register.note: Credit lines, sustainability-linked bonds and partial credit guarantees
register.text: Additional IDA financing for working capital and investment credit lines, a sustainability-linked bond programme and partial credit guarantees, channelled through the Development Bank of Rwanda. By December 2025, 9,597 firms had benefited from the project’s credit facilities, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation, second additional financing
register.detail: Approved 27 March 2026 · IDA · Closing 28 February 2029
register.note: Extends farm finance to 2029
register.text: A second top-up to the agricultural transformation project of 2022, which draws private finance into farming and agribusiness. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: First Inclusive and Resilient Job Creation Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 23 March 2026 · IDA credit of JPY 15.4 billion · Policy-based guarantee of $240 million · First of a series of three
register.note: With a $240 million guarantee for up to $450 million of commercial loans
register.text: Budget support for reforms in revenue, public-private partnerships and state-owned enterprises, shared broadband infrastructure, Ejo Heza savings, skills and job matching, and farming and aquaculture. Its guarantee helps Rwanda raise up to $450 million of commercial financing on favourable terms.

register.name: Revenue Improvement and Spending Efficiency Program-for-Results
register.detail: Approved 21 November 2025 · IDA
register.note: National ministries, state-owned companies and all 30 districts
register.text: Results-based financing to raise domestic revenue and make public spending more efficient, with national ministries, state-owned companies and all 30 districts as direct beneficiaries. Revenue of its own widens what Rwanda can spend on the seven standards.

register.name: Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: Approved 30 September 2025 · Funds that can be drawn after a disaster
register.note: About 40% of the population lives in high-risk highland areas
register.text: Supports reforms in disaster risk information and coordination, the resilience of the built environment and the management of natural resources, with funds Rwanda can draw quickly after a disaster. The floods and landslides of May 2023 left over 18,000 people homeless; the operation protects the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Boosting Green Finance, Investment and Trade
register.detail: Approved 20 December 2024 · Three IDA credits, fully disbursed · Closed 20 December 2025
register.note: Policy reforms for green finance
register.text: Supports reforms that open Rwanda to green investment and trade.

register.name: Priority Skills for Growth and Youth Empowerment
register.detail: Approved 9 September 2024 · IDA
register.note: Skills and jobs for more than 200,000 youths
register.text: Pays on verified results in technical training and youth employment, for more than 200,000 young people.

register.name: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience
register.detail: Approved 24 May 2024 · Multiphase programmatic approach · Closing 31 March 2030
register.note: Health security
register.text: Strengthens the health system against outbreaks.

register.name: Standby Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 14 December 2023 · 14 months
register.note: Balance-of-payments support
register.text: Short-term support approved alongside the PCI and RSF reviews, completed December 2024.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation
register.detail: Approved 28 November 2023 · Two IDA credits · Closing 31 December 2029
register.note: Electricity and clean cooking access
register.text: Extends electricity and clean cooking to households. It is aimed at the energy standard, where 9% of Rwandans cook with clean fuels and technology, which sets Rwanda’s Coverage. By 1 December 2025 it had brought electricity to 70,500 people, against a target of 1,880,000 by December 2029.

register.name: Congo Nile Divide forest and landscape restoration (FP217)
register.detail: Approved 25 October 2023 · Grant · Accredited entity: Ministry of Environment · Effective 20 February 2024
register.note: 250,000 hectares of land
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant to build the resilience of vulnerable communities on the Congo Nile Divide through forest and landscape restoration across 250,000 hectares, with agroforestry on 2,000 hectares. It protects the soil and water behind the food and water standards.

register.name: Stunting Prevention and Reduction, Additional Financing
register.detail: Additional financing, 2023 · IDA credit of $70 million and grants of $9 million
register.note: Child nutrition
register.text: Works to reduce stunting among young children.

register.name: Policy Coordination Instrument
register.detail: Approved 12 December 2022 · Sixth and final review 4 December 2025
register.note: A non-financing programme that signals policy to investors
register.text: A non-financing IMF instrument that signals the strength of policies to investors and partners. It was completed with its sixth and final review in December 2025.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Approved 12 December 2022 · Final review 13 December 2024
register.note: Long-term financing tied to climate reforms
register.text: One of the first RSF arrangements in the world, completed in full.

register.name: Social Protection Transformation Project
register.detail: Approved 22 September 2022 · IDA · Closing 31 December 2026
register.note: Safety nets
register.text: Modernises the cash transfer and public works system for the poorest households.

register.name: Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation
register.detail: Approved 15 April 2022 · IDA · Amounts revised since approval; second additional financing of $80 million in March 2026
register.note: Finance for farms and agribusiness
register.text: Draws private finance into farming and the businesses around it.

register.name: Housing Finance Project
register.detail: Approved 29 November 2018 · IDA credit of EUR 129.6 million · Closed 31 October 2025
register.note: 17,845 housing loans against a target of 6,000
register.text: Built the market for long-term, affordable home loans. It financed 17,845 housing loans against a target of 6,000 and closed in October 2025 with an outcome rated Satisfactory.

register.name: Volcanoes Community Resilience Project
register.detail: Financing agreement signed, announced 5 August 2026 · Eight districts
register.note: More than 2.3 million people in areas exposed to floods and landslides
register.text: European Investment Bank finance for flood risk reduction, watershed restoration, landscape rehabilitation, biodiversity and livelihoods in Gakenke, Burera, Musanze, Nyabihu, Rubavu, Rutsiro, Ngororero and Muhanga. It protects the shelter, water and livelihood standards for more than 2.3 million people.

register.name: Energy Sector Results Based Financing Phase II (RBF II)
register.detail: Launched 15 May 2026 · Implemented through the Rwanda Energy Group · $300 million programme with $100 million from AIIB
register.note: 200,000 households to the grid and clean cooking for 100,000
register.text: An African Development Bank loan that pays on results for 200,000 new household grid connections, 50,000 off-grid connections and clean cooking devices for 100,000 households and 310 public institutions. It is aimed at the energy standard, which sets Rwanda’s Coverage.

register.name: Muvumba Multipurpose Water Resources Development Program, additional financing
register.detail: Announced 16 April 2026 · €17.66 million African Development Fund loan and €27.74 million African Development Bank loan · Programme value €176 million
register.note: Bank Group contribution now €166.9 million
register.text: Additional finance for the Muvumba dam programme, including a climate-resilient irrigation system for 3,073 hectares of farmland. The dam develops water for several uses, including power, farming and water for people, serving the water, food and energy standards.

register.name: Rwanda Energy Results-Based Financing Program
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 · Sovereign · Co-financed with the African Development Bank, the lead co-financier
register.note: AIIB’s share of the $300 million programme
register.text: An AIIB loan that co-finances the African Development Bank’s results-based programme for grid and off-grid connections and clean cooking. It is aimed at the energy standard, which sets Rwanda’s Coverage.

register.name: Karenge water project and SME credit line
register.detail: Signed 8 October 2025 · $20 million loan for the Karenge Water Project · $25 million line of credit to the Development Bank of Rwanda
register.note: Two agreements with the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa
register.text: One loan expands the transmission and distribution systems of the Karenge Water Project, supporting the goal of universal clean water and sanitation by 2029; the other lends to small and medium enterprises through the Development Bank of Rwanda. They serve the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: HANGARIBIHE: climate-smart and inclusive agriculture
register.detail: Signed 4 August 2026 · EUR 36 million budget support and EUR 4 million technical assistance · Five years
register.note: Smallholders, cooperatives, women, youth and SMEs
register.text: A European Union financing agreement, mostly budget support, for climate-smart and inclusive agriculture. It serves the food and livelihood standards for smallholders, cooperatives, women, youth and small businesses.

register.name: Inclusive social protection grant
register.detail: Signed 6 October 2025 · Grant · Implemented by the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency
register.note: Supports the Vision Umurenge Program
register.text: A German grant through KfW to strengthen Rwanda’s inclusive social protection system and its flagship Vision Umurenge Program. It serves the livelihood standard for the poorest households.

register.name: Development Policy Loan for the Education Sector
register.detail: Signed 5 March 2024, Kigali · 0.20% a year · 40 years, including 10 years’ grace
register.note: Up to 14,000 million yen
register.text: A Japanese loan to improve children’s learning, with stronger teacher training colleges, more classrooms, pre-primary education, school lunches and digital education. It serves the education standard.

register.name: BPR Bank Rwanda, local-currency loan
register.detail: Approved 28 June 2024 · Signed 9 August 2024 · Invested 30 December 2024 · Seven years, in Rwandan francs · Up to $60 million with $20 million mobilized
register.note: At least 25% for women-owned SMEs
register.text: An IFC loan to Rwanda’s third-largest bank by assets for lending to small and medium enterprises, backed by the IDA20 Private Sector Window local currency facility. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Bank of Kigali, green agriculture value chain loan
register.detail: Signed 14 March 2024 · On-lending to small and medium enterprises
register.note: Agriculture value chains
register.text: A European Investment Bank loan to Bank of Kigali for on-lending to small and medium enterprises in agricultural value chains. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Hills
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Three-quarters of the land is farmed. Irrigation and markets, not more land, carry the next gain.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: The forest holds the water for the hills below and the parks that visitors come for.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Tourism revenue, 2025
items.text: 1.49 million arrivals in 2025, up 9% on the year before.
items.alt: Visitors in a Rwandan national park

items.name: The Hub
items.label: Investment registered, 2025
items.text: Across 799 projects. A state that investors can read is itself an asset.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Three in ten live in towns and cities; the rest live on the hills they farm.

items.name: One Acre Fund (Tubura)
items.text: Has operated in Rwanda since 2007 under the local brand Tubura and serves 2.7 million farmers. It distributed 25.6 million tree seedlings in 2024.

items.name: Kigali Bulk Water (Metito)
items.text: Metito designed, built and operates the $61 million Kigali bulk water plant, which supplies the national utility with 40,000 cubic metres of potable water a day and raised the city’s supply by 40 percent.

items.name: DelAgua
items.text: Has run a clean cookstove programme in Rwanda since 2012, funded by the sale of carbon credits, with over 1.9 million stoves distributed. In November 2025 TotalEnergies agreed to fund 200,000 more within one year.

items.name: Kepler
items.text: Offers bachelor’s degrees with Southern New Hampshire University in Kigali and at the Kiziba refugee camp. By October 2023, 957 students had earned degrees, including 237 refugees.

items.name: Zipline
items.text: Delivers blood to hospitals by drone: 28,754 units in Rwanda in 2023. A 2023 study by researchers at the Wharton School, with the Ministry of Health, found that it reduced nationwide in-hospital deaths from postpartum haemorrhage by 51%.

items.name: BPR Bank Rwanda
items.text: Rwanda’s third-largest bank by assets, on-lending a seven-year IFC package of up to $60 million in Rwandan francs to small and medium enterprises, with at least 25 percent for women-owned firms.

coverage.gap_text: Rwandans who cook without clean fuel or technology: nine in ten.
